error_types.alias_duplicate: An existing payee is paid again under a different identity string (name variant and/or new email). Two sub-cases: 'both' (canonical row AND alias row are in the batch) and 'drift' (only the alias row is in the batch; canonical was paid in earlier batches).
error_types.email_typo: Name is correct but the email has exactly one character edit (substitution, deletion, insertion or adjacent transposition) relative to the payee's known email.
error_types.exact_duplicate: A row is repeated verbatim (same record, same amount, same note) in the batch.
error_types.amount_outlier: Amount multiplied by a decimal-shift factor (x10, x100, /10, /100) or a random high/low factor. Only injected for payees with >=3 prior payouts (otherwise undetectable by design).

alias_kinds.initial: first name reduced to an initial
alias_kinds.nickname: formal first name replaced by a nickname (table in names.py)
alias_kinds.typo_name: one character edit in first or last name
alias_kinds.honorific: title or generational suffix added (normalises away)
alias_kinds.email_change: a new unrelated email address (new domain and/or pattern)
alias_kinds.email_variant: same mailbox written differently (+tag, dots, trailing digits)

notes: difficulty=hard: alias records are 70% name+email changes, lose/alter country (50%) and drift in amount (lognormal 0.5); hard-negative rates doubled.
History is clean except for 'history identity drift' (~20% of persons, ~10% of businesses are legitimately paid under two records); those are true same-entity pairs but not injected errors.
Hard negatives: relatives (same surname/domain), look-alike names (one-edit), homonyms (same name).
Amounts are not currency-converted; per-payee spread is 0 (fixed fee, 35%), small or larger.
